designs.understanding: research/sources.py has one Cache class with two tiers (Redis rs:{sha1}, disk {sha1}.json) and _get_json builds the key as 'GET {url} {params-json}'. That one string is doing four jobs (identity of the request, cache key, future lock key, warming key) and it is wrong for all of them: it includes api_key (papers() and paper_count() put the OpenAlex key into params), it is the exact query text so registry-driven warming never produces a founder's key, and it carries no source in the Redis name. The storage around it has no metadata: a disk file is the raw body, so the code cannot know its age except via mtime (and forgets it when promoting to Redis with a full TTL), cannot store a status (so EPO's 404-means-none is never cached), and is written in place with write_text (a truncated file makes json.loads raise inside aget, failing the whole scan for up to 7 days). Coordination is absent: no single-flight in the default one-process setup, and the planned Redis lock (30 s) is shorter than one 60 s httpx call. core/redis.py memoises a failed ping forever (reset_redis has no caller), so Redis that starts late is never used and per-layer counters cannot tell 'off' from 'cold'. Finally the ~25 @lru_cache reference loaders have no record of which datasets they read, so 2.2.3's per-loader clear would leave get_ecosystem() holding old banking branch counts. Root cause in one line: research responses have no request identity and no envelope, and cached reference data has no dataset identity.

approaches.name: Harden the existing two-tier cache: canonical request identity + envelope + atomic writes + two-level single-flight + demand-driven refresh-ahead + dataset cache registry
approaches.how: A RequestKey (source, url, params minus credential params) is the single identity for cache, lock, demand log and warming. Disk and Redis store a small envelope {v, status, fetched_at, req, body}; disk writes go to a temp file then os.replace; unreadable files are a miss and are deleted. Promotion to Redis uses the remaining TTL. A per-source cacheable-status set lets EPO 404 be cached as empty. In-process asyncio futures give single-flight without Redis; redis.asyncio Lock (token-safe, timeout from the httpx timeout) adds cross-process single-flight. get_redis re-probes after a back-off. A demand log of request keys drives refresh-ahead with a warming share of the budget. A @dataset_cache decorator records which datasets each lru_cache loader reads.
approaches.basis: Standard library (hashlib, os.replace, asyncio) and redis-py, which is already a dependency; refresh-ahead and single-flight are well-known cache patterns (Go singleflight, Caffeine refreshAfterWrite).
approaches.advantages: No new dependency, keeps decisions 0003/0010 and SYSTEM-DESIGN §4 two-tier layout, keeps the budget and 429 pause logic in the same function, fixes every flag at the root (identity + envelope).
approaches.drawbacks: Hand-written code to maintain (~200 lines); the envelope is a small on-disk format change that needs a legacy read path.

approaches.name: hishel (RFC 9111 HTTP cache transport for httpx)
approaches.how: Wrap the httpx.AsyncClient in hishel's AsyncCacheTransport with a file or Redis storage; caching decisions follow HTTP cache headers or a forced policy.
approaches.basis: Mature, popular httpx companion; file, Redis and SQLite storages.
approaches.advantages: Atomic storage and standard semantics for free; keys can exclude headers.
approaches.drawbacks: Caches below _get_json, so budget counting, the 429 pause and status-based negative caching need re-plumbing; OpenAlex/EPO send little useful cache metadata so a forced TTL policy is needed anyway; a second cache layer beside the existing one; no single-flight.

approaches.name: diskcache (SQLite-backed cache) as the disk tier
approaches.how: Replace the JSON file tier with diskcache.Cache(expire=ttl); use its memoize_stampede / Lock recipes for coordination.
approaches.basis: Mature pure-Python library, process-safe, used widely.
approaches.advantages: Atomic writes, expiry and eviction built in, process-safe locks across workers on one host.
approaches.drawbacks: New dependency and a data migration; synchronous API inside async code (needs to_thread); locks are per host only, so Redis still needed for several hosts; stores opaque blobs that operators cannot inspect as easily as JSON files.

approaches.name: aiocache with memory and Redis backends
approaches.how: Decorate the connectors with aiocache.cached using a Redis backend and a memory fallback; key builder strips credentials.
approaches.advantages: Async-native; pluggable key builders and serializers.
approaches.drawbacks: No durable disk tier (memory fallback is lost on restart, which is the offline default), so the 7-day cache disappears without Redis; rewrites the cache to fix what are mostly identity and coordination problems.

approaches.name: PostgreSQL table as the research cache (research_cache(key, status, fetched_at, body jsonb))
approaches.how: Store responses in a table with an index on key and fetched_at; use advisory locks for single-flight.
approaches.basis: SQLAlchemy 2 and Alembic are in the stack; advisory locks are a known single-flight tool.
approaches.advantages: Transactional writes, queryable demand, works across workers and hosts.
approaches.drawbacks: Blocked on the database being reachable (2.1.1) and breaks the offline baseline where only disk exists; puts high-churn cache rows in the system of record.

approaches.name: Static nightly warming from registry domain queries (the current 2.2.6 plan)
approaches.how: For each of 240 registry domains, run its research queries nightly under the daily cap.
approaches.drawbacks: The reviewer's probe shows the warmed keys do not match founder keys (different words, different params), and it spends the shared cap and re-fetches entries still valid for 7 days.

designs.chosen: Harden the existing two-tier cache: canonical request identity + envelope + atomic writes + two-level single-flight + demand-driven refresh-ahead + dataset cache registry
designs.why_chosen: Every symptom traces back to two missing pieces of data: a request identity without secrets, and stored metadata (status, fetched_at, the replayable request). Adding both inside the existing Cache fixes key rotation, double TTL, negative caching, truncated files and warming in one place, with only the standard library and redis-py, and keeps the budget/pause checks where they are. In-process futures make single-flight work in the default one-process setup (decision 0010), and redis-py's Lock covers several workers without new code. Refresh-ahead from real demand is the only warming that hits founders' keys.

not_chosen.reason: A second cache under the existing one; it bypasses the per-source budget and 429 pause and still needs a forced TTL and custom keying, so it adds a dependency without removing our code.

not_chosen.name: diskcache
not_chosen.reason: New dependency plus a migration to fix atomicity that os.replace fixes in three lines; sync API in async code; still needs Redis for cross-host locks.

not_chosen.name: aiocache
not_chosen.reason: Loses the disk tier, which is the only cache in the free offline setup.

not_chosen.name: PostgreSQL cache table
not_chosen.reason: Blocked on 2.1.1 and fails the offline baseline; cache churn does not belong in the system of record.

not_chosen.name: Static registry warming
not_chosen.reason: Proven to warm keys founders never request while spending their shared budget.

design.components: 1) research/cache_key.py: RequestKey(source, method, url, params) with CREDENTIAL_PARAMS = {'api_key','mailto','key','token','access_token'} stripped; .digest() = sha1 of the canonical string 'GET {url} {json.dumps(params_wo_creds, sort_keys=True)}' (identical to today's string when no key is set, so today's disk entries stay valid); .redis_key() = 'rs:{source}:{digest}' (aligns 2.2.2). 2) Cache (research/sources.py) stores Envelope {v:1, status, fetched_at (epoch s), req {url, params}, body}; get() reads legacy raw files as status 200 with fetched_at = mtime; corrupt/unreadable file -> log cache.corrupt with the file name, unlink, return miss; put() writes '{name}.{pid}.{rand}.tmp' then os.replace; Redis promotion uses ex = ttl - age (skip when <= 0). 3) CACHEABLE_STATUS per source: default {200}, epo {200, 404} (404 stored as status 404 with body None; epo_patents already maps 404 to (0, [])). 4) SingleFlight: dict[digest, asyncio.Future] in-process; with Redis, an outer redis.asyncio.lock.Lock('lock:{source}:{digest}', timeout=http_timeout+10, blocking_timeout=http_timeout+15). Order: cache -> join in-process flight -> Redis lock -> re-check cache -> pause -> budget -> fetch -> store -> release. Waiters re-run the cache and pause checks after waking, never the fetch blindly. 5) core/redis.py: failure memo becomes (None, retry_at); re-probe after settings.redis_retry_s (60 s); redis_state() -> 'off' | 'up' | 'down'; counters cache_stats {redis_hit, disk_hit, miss, redis_down_reads} for 5.4.2. 6) Demand log: every founder-originated lookup (hit or miss) records its digest: Redis ZINCRBY 'rs:demand:{yyyy-mm-dd}' (TTL 8 days) or, without Redis, an append-only line in {cache_dir}/demand/{date}.log. 7) Budget caller class: _over_budget(source, caller='founder'|'warm'); warm may use at most research_warm_share (0.25) of the per-source cap (T15 owns the per-source cap table) and, when no cap is set, at most research_warm_max per source per night. 8) scripts/warm_research_cache.py (nightly, 5.4.4): digests demanded >= 2 times in the last 7 days whose envelope expires within 36 h, replayed from envelope.req with caller='warm', most-demanded first, stopping at the warm budget; it never refetches a fresh entry. 9) core/datasets.py: @dataset_cache('banking', 'ecosystem') wraps functools.lru_cache and registers fn -> datasets; clear(dataset) clears every loader that declared it; version(dataset) = sha1 of the data files' (size, mtime) for 2.2.3 and the 2.2.4 ETag.
design.data_model: Envelope JSON {"v":1,"status":200|404,"fetched_at":1760000000,"req":{"url":...,"params":{...without credentials}},"body":...}. Redis keys: rs:{source}:{digest} (EX remaining ttl), lock:{source}:{digest}, rs:neg:{source} (pause, unchanged meaning), rs:demand:{date} (ZSET digest->count), budget:{source}:{date}:{caller}. DATASETS registry: dict[str, set[Callable]] plus DATA_FILES: dict[str, list[Path]].
design.algorithm: lookup(req, caller): k=RequestKey(req); env=cache.get(k) -> if env and fresh: record_demand(k) if caller=='founder'; return env. fut=flights.get(k): if fut: return await fut. Create fut; try: async with redis_lock(k) (or nullcontext): env=cache.get(k); if env: resolve; if paused(source): resolve 429; if over_budget(source, caller): resolve 429; r=await http; if r.status in CACHEABLE_STATUS[source]: cache.put(k, Envelope(...)); if 429: pause(); resolve (status, body) finally: flights.pop(k). Remaining TTL on promotion: ttl - (now - fetched_at).
design.interfaces: T15 (A3) owns per-source limits and the per-source status vocabulary; T08 adds the caller dimension and the RequestKey that T15's counters use. T13 relies on SourceResult statuses staying honest (a cached 404 is 'ok, 0 found', a budget refusal is 'budget_exhausted'). T33 eval fixtures can be recorded as envelopes (req + status + body) and replayed, including degraded statuses. T23 reads cache_stats and redis_state. 2.2.3 (version key) and 2.2.4 (ETags) call datasets.clear/version. T32's maintenance runner calls Cache.purge() and the warmer.
files: backend/app/ecosystem/index.py and the ~25 lru_cache loaders (decorator swap)
design.rollout: Step 1 (no behaviour risk): RequestKey + envelope with legacy read + atomic write + remaining TTL + EPO 404; existing disk entries remain valid because the canonical string equals today's when no key is set. Step 2: single-flight (in-process first, Redis lock second) and the Redis re-probe. Step 3: dataset registry (mechanical decorator swap, one PR per package). Step 4: demand log, then the warmer once 2.2.6's key is in place. Old Redis rs:{hash} keys simply expire within 7 days.
design.offline: Without Redis everything still works: disk tier with atomic envelopes, in-process single-flight, in-process budget counters, a local demand log; the warmer reads the local logs. Without network, cached envelopes still answer and misses report 'error' or 'budget_exhausted' honestly.

design.data_model: SupplyMapLineOut {line, makers: [DirectoryRow], traders: int, gap: bool, gap_reason: str|null, cluster: {place, district, km, source_url}|null, coverage: {...}}. DirectoryRow adds distance_basis: 'pin' | 'district_centroid' | null. QuoteIn adds delivery_per_unit: float|None (>=0). Allocation response adds alternatives: [{line, supplier_id, buy: moq, extra_units, cost}] and rules: {preference_band_pct, landed_cost: 'price + your delivery cost'}.
design.algorithm: Allocation: model M with x, y, short as today. Stage 1: maximise sum(x); P* = value. Stage 2: add sum(x) == P*; minimise sum(landed_paise * x); C* = value. designs.understanding: Every reader of founder text works on raw strings with no notion of tokens, spans or scope. extract._first_cue uses 'n in low' (plain substring), so 'app' fires inside Tiruchirappalli/happily/apparel and 'crop' inside microprocessor, at confidence 0.90/0.70 that is never questioned. answers._stage takes the first stage whose word appears, revenue first, with no negation ('no customers yet' -> revenue, stored as an ANSWER at 0.90). places.find_district does use letter boundaries but returns the longest name anywhere in the text, so position and negation are ignored ('Salem not Madurai' -> madurai, 'live in Salem, sell in Coimbatore' -> coimbatore), and it knows only 38 districts plus ~25 aliases, no towns (Pollachi, Kumbakonam). At the restatement, ideation._advance turns the reply into a bag of words: YES contains 'right', NO contains 'not', and 'not right' contains both, so it confirms; a 'yes, but ...' correction is never observed; and engine.confirm takes only a bool, so a 'no' that names the fix stores the rejected value (via the negation-blind extractor) and loops on the same restatement. Finally extract emits a positional 'problem' guess (first sentence, 0.55) for any 25+ char reply, and engine.observe only skips the slot being answered, so a long answer to the beneficiary question overwrites the problem. Root cause: there is no shared utterance reader that returns typed mentions with position and polarity, and no correction operation in the engine.

approaches.name: Shared rule-based utterance reader: boundary-aware cue sets, a NegEx-style negation window, a correction grammar, positional place resolution and a cited town gazetteer
approaches.how: One module tokenises with character spans; CueSets compile word-boundary regexes (explicit stem* marker for prefixes like manufactur*); each hit carries span and a negated flag from a short trigger window (no, not, never, without, n't, illai, yet-to) closed by scope breakers (but, comma, however, actually); a correction parser recognises 'X not Y', 'not Y, X', 'actually X', 'instead of Y', 'change Y to X'; place mentions are resolved by polarity, role cue (in/from/based vs sell to/market) and position; a town->district gazetteer from the India Post directory adds towns.
approaches.basis: NegEx (Chapman et al. 2001) is the standard rule approach to negation scope, widely used in clinical NLP; word-boundary regex and gazetteers are the established baseline for slot filling; India Post data is already cited in the repo.
approaches.advantages: Offline, deterministic, explainable, works on Tanglish with a few Tamil triggers, testable against the eval set; fits decision 0002 (code decides).
approaches.drawbacks: Rules need curation and a negative-case corpus; free word order and unusual phrasing will still be missed and must fall back to a question.

approaches.advantages: Robust tokenisation, lemmas, ready negation component.
approaches.drawbacks: Adds a large dependency and a model download (en_core_web_sm), English-only (Tamil/Tanglish replies), and the negation and correction logic still has to be written for our slots.

design.components: 1) elicitation/reader.py: tokens(text) -> list[Tok(text, low, start, end, i)]; CueSet(mapping value->cues) compiled to one alternation regex with (?<!\w) / (?!\w) boundaries, 'stem*' for prefixes, optional plural s; find(text) -> list[Mention(value, cue, start, end, negated)] ordered by position. 2) Negation: PRE triggers {no, not, never, without, none, nothing, nobody, don't, doesn't, didn't, haven't, hasn't, isn't, aren't, wasn't, can't, won't, yet to, illai, illa, alla}; window = up to 4 tokens after the trigger, closed by breakers {but, however, though, actually, instead, ',', ';', '.'}; pseudo-negations {not only, no doubt, not just} ignored; POST triggers {not yet} within 2 tokens after a mention. 3) places.py: find_places(text) -> list[PlaceMention(district, candidates, name, start, end, negated, role, via)]; role = 'home' after {in, at, from, based in, live in, unit in, near} | 'market' after {sell in, sell to, market in, supply to, customers in} | None; via in {district, alias, town}. resolve_district(mentions, corrected_span=None): drop negated; prefer a mention inside a correction's new-value span; then role home; then first by position; role market never fills district. 4) elicitation/data/tn_towns.json: {town: district | [districts]} from the India Post all-India pincode directory (data.gov.in, the source already used by scripts/build_ecosystem.py), S.O/H.O office names with suffixes stripped, generic names removed via a reviewed exclusion list; built by scripts/build_town_gazetteer.py with _meta {source, retrieved, rows, ambiguous}. Ambiguous towns return candidates, never a guess. 5) elicitation/corrections.py: parse_corrections(text, filled_slots) -> list[Correction(slot, new_value|None, rejected_value|None, span)]; patterns per slot type use the reader: places, sector/form CueSets, stage cues, money. 'not Y' alone -> rejected Y, new None. 6) elicitation/confirmation.py: read_reply(text) -> Verdict in {AFFIRM, REJECT, AFFIRM_WITH_CHANGES, UNCLEAR} using negation-aware YES/NO cue sets ('not right', 'not correct' -> REJECT) plus corrections. 7) engine.confirm(session, verdict, corrections): AFFIRM and no corrections -> generate; any correction -> apply as founder corrections (T03 source 'correction', locked), stay CONFIRMING and restate the changed objective ('Got it, Salem. So: ...'); REJECT without corrections -> Action(kind='ask_which', options=[restated facts]) rendered as a question by voice and as chips on screen; UNCLEAR -> repeat the restatement once, then ask_which. 8) extract.py: all cue lists become CueSets compiled from T01's canonical vocabulary; negated sector/form/stage mentions are not emitted (negated stage mentions are returned as excluded values for the selector); positional 'problem' guess flagged positional=True. 9) engine.observe: run parse_corrections first in every state, apply them as corrections; skip positional extractions when answering a slot other than problem; session.put rule (with T03): a positional guess never replaces an existing value. 10) answers._stage: CueSet + negation; negated revenue/growth cues never return revenue; if only negated cues match, return None so the question is re-asked with the remaining options.
design.data_model: Mention(value, cue, start, end, negated: bool). PlaceMention(district: str|None, candidates: list[str], name, start, end, negated, role, via). Correction(slot: str, new_value: Any|None, rejected_value: Any|None, span: tuple[int,int]). Verdict enum. Action gains kind 'ask_which' with options: list[{slot, label, value}]. tn_towns.json {"_meta": {...}, "towns": {"pollachi": "coimbatore", "kumbakonam": "thanjavur", "<ambiguous>": ["a","b"]}}.
design.algorithm: Negation: for each mention m, look back over tokens before m.start until a breaker or 4 tokens; negated if a PRE trigger is found and it is not part of a pseudo-negation; also negated if a POST trigger follows within 2 tokens. Correction grammar (applied on spans): 'A not B' / 'A, not B' -> new A, rejected B (same slot type); 'not B, (it is|its|but) A' -> same; 'actually|sorry|I mean A' -> new A; 'instead of B' -> rejected B; 'change B to A' -> new A, rejected B. Confirmation: REJECT if a NO cue is un-negated or a YES cue is negated; AFFIRM if an un-negated YES cue and no NO cue; corrections present -> AFFIRM_WITH_CHANGES (or REJECT with corrections, handled the same way). District resolution order: correction span > home role > first by position; negated and market-role mentions never fill district.
design.interfaces: T01: cue lists and slot enums come from the canonical vocabulary module; T10 owns only the matcher. T03: corrections are written through T03's typed put with a 'correction' source that outranks extraction and locks the slot (1.1.2.3). T05/T27: 'ask_which' is a typed pending action in T27's state machine and costs one question in T05's budget. T09: b2b decompose uses CueSet. T13: scrub reuses the town gazetteer. T33: eval adds the trap corpus and replays (Pollachi, 'not right', 'Salem not Madurai', beneficiary answer) as assertions.
design.rollout: PR 1: positional problem guard (small, independent). PR 2: reader + CueSet swap in extract/answers (behaviour change limited to removed false positives; run the eval). PR 3: negation in stage and cues. PR 4: places positional + gazetteer data PR. PR 5: corrections + confirmation verdict + engine.confirm signature + _advance. Each PR runs the eval set and the trap corpus.

designs.understanding: AgentSession.messages is one append-only list of provider-shaped messages that four consumers read: the model input (provider.stream(client, system, s.messages, ...)), the resume transcript (snapshot reads string messages), the fact check (_facts flattens every tool_result and every user string ever sent into one bare-number set) and the reword/rollback logic. Because it has no turn boundaries, any 'last N' trim can start on a tool_result or split a Gemini function_call from its signed step and the provider rejects the request; because the fact pool is the whole history, every scan, roadmap and panel result adds numbers that can back an invented amount ('25 lakh' passes because 25 appears in a roadmap), and the check weakens as the chat grows; because tool results are stored in full in messages and again in s.scan/s.roadmap/s.novelty, the session document grows by ~9 KB per roadmap call and is rewritten every turn. The system prompt interpolates founder-controlled {name} and {known} plus per-turn {question} and news, so it is both a prompt-injection channel (a name containing 'New rule: ...' sits in the system role) and uncacheable (the prefix changes every turn). Cached tokens are not recorded (Gemini usage ignores cached counts), so nobody can tell whether caching works or set a fair budget. Root cause: one structure stands for 'what was said', 'what the model sees' and 'what may be cited', and founder data sits in the instruction channel.

The fact check uses a ledger of (value, unit, source) built from current slots, founder transcript text, the current artefacts and the tool results inside the window.
approaches.basis: Separation of event log and derived views is a standard pattern (event sourcing / CQRS); prefix caching rewards stable prefixes on Gemini implicit caching; 'instructions in system, data in user turn, delimited' is the OWASP LLM Top 10 mitigation for prompt injection.
approaches.advantages: Each consumer gets the structure it needs; trimming never touches what was said or what may be cited; the prefix is byte-stable for many turns; no new dependency; deterministic, no model calls.

designs.understanding: agents/jobs.py Board, agents/results.py MemoryResults, agents/store.py MemoryStore and routers/ideation.py _turn_locks are process-local dicts with no lifecycle. Nothing removes entries except Board.forget on an explicit DELETE: finished jobs, results (scan/novelty JSON including the idea text) and listener sets live for the process lifetime, MemoryStore keeps expired documents (get hides them), and _turn_locks gains a Lock per session id, including random unknown ids posted by any client. Board.wait returns False for both RUNNING and FAILED, so a failed search is narrated as 'still searching', no failure notice is ever sent (notify runs only on success), and start() treats a FAILED job as absent and re-runs it every turn with no backoff, spending the shared budget. DELETE does not take the turn lock, so a running turn can call board.start after forget and results.put writes results for a deleted session. The streaming route acquires the lock before returning StreamingResponse and releases it in the generator's finally, which never runs if the body is never iterated, leaving the session locked. There is no concurrency limit, so a burst of sessions starts unbounded parallel scans. Root cause: in-process state has no owner that applies the session's lifetime and no explicit job outcome model.

approaches.name: Session lifecycle registry in process: explicit job outcomes with failure notices and backoff, per-kind concurrency limits, tombstones on delete, ref-counted turn locks acquired inside the stream, and an idle sweep tied to the store's expiry; durable rows later cascade from agent_sessions
approaches.how: One module owns per-session in-process state and applies the session idle expiry from T07's store contract. Jobs carry attempts and a terminal outcome; wait returns the outcome; failures notify listeners and back off; semaphores bound concurrent jobs; delete writes a tombstone that start/put refuse, cancels jobs and waits for the turn lock; locks exist only while held or awaited; a sweep (lifespan task plus opportunistic call on create) removes idle rows, finished jobs, empty listener sets and expired MemoryStore documents.
approaches.basis: Plain asyncio primitives (Task, Semaphore, Lock) and the existing Board interface; ref-counted keyed locks are a standard keyed-mutex pattern; tombstones are the standard guard against write-after-delete.
approaches.advantages: No dependency, works in the offline single-process baseline today, keeps decision 0010's job board, and the same contract (outcome states, tombstone, cascade) carries over to 2.3.1's Redis queue and table.

design.components: 1) agents/lifecycle.py (new): SessionLocks with acquire(session_id, timeout=None) as an async context manager over dict[str, (Lock, waiters)]; the entry is created on first acquire and removed when the holder releases with zero waiters, so the map holds only active sessions. Tombstones: dict[str, expires_at] with TTL = T07 idle expiry; is_forgotten(id). touch(id) records last activity. sweep(now) removes everything idle beyond the expiry. 2) agents/jobs.py: Outcome = Literal['done','running','failed','none']; Job gains attempts, finished_at, reason ('timeout', 'source_error', 'budget', from T15 when available) and retry_at; wait() returns Outcome; start() refuses a session that is_forgotten, returns the failed job instead of restarting it until retry_at (backoff 30 s, 2 min, 10 min; max 3 attempts per idea version, reset when the idea version changes, T06); run() re-checks is_forgotten before results.put and notify; per-kind asyncio.Semaphore (settings.job_concurrency_research=4, council=2) taken inside run(); notify_failure sends {'kind','state':'failed','reason','retry_at'}. 3) agents/results.py: MemoryResults rows store (written_at, touched_at, payload); get/latest update touched_at; sweep(cutoff) drops rows untouched since cutoff; latest() uses a per-session index instead of scanning every row. 4) agents/store.py MemoryStore: get() pops an expired document; sweep() pops all expired documents. 5) routers/ideation.py: agent_turn and agent_turn_stream use lifecycle locks; the stream route does a lock-free _load (404 for unknown ids, no lock entry created), then acquires the lock inside the generator and reloads; agent_delete: tombstone -> board.forget (cancel jobs, drop results, close listeners) -> acquire the turn lock with a timeout (5 s) -> store.delete; the notices stream emits a 'failed' SSE event. 6) ideation.py: _search/_convene/offline paths branch on Outcome; 'failed' is narrated once per attempt from a template ('I could not search this time: <reason>. I will try again in a few minutes, or ask me to retry.'), recorded in s.narrated; never 'still searching' for a failed job. 7) main.py lifespan: start an asyncio task calling lifecycle.sweep every settings.sweep_interval_s (600 s) and cancel it on shutdown; agent_start also calls sweep opportunistically every 100 creates (covers tests and servers without lifespan). 8) 2.3.1 spec: agent_results(session_id FK -> agent_sessions ON DELETE CASCADE, idea_version, kind, payload, written_at); 3.2.4 retention and erasure lists name results.
design.data_model: Job {session_id, kind, task, started, attempts, finished_at, outcome, reason, retry_at}. MemoryResults row {(session, version, kind): (written_at, touched_at, payload_json)}. Tombstones {session_id: expires_at}. Lock map {session_id: (asyncio.Lock, waiters:int)}. Notice event 'failed' {kind, reason, retry_at}.
design.algorithm: Delete: tombstone(id); await board.forget(id) (cancel, drop, close); try: async with locks.acquire(id, timeout=5): await store.delete(id) except timeout: await store.delete(id) (the running turn's save then fails its version check and is discarded). Start: if forgotten -> None; current failed and now < retry_at -> return current; else new task. Sweep: cutoff = now - idle_expiry; drop finished jobs with finished_at < cutoff, results with touched_at < cutoff, listener entries with empty sets, tombstones past expiry, MemoryStore documents expired; running jobs are never removed.

T23 exposes gauges (jobs, results rows, locks, tombstones). T32 owns durable retention/erasure and lists agent_results; its maintenance runner is the external counterpart for disk/DB/Redis, while this sweep owns process memory. T15 supplies the failure reason vocabulary for research jobs. T11 artefacts are where taken results land in the session.

Delete race: start a turn that blocks inside a tool, DELETE, then let the turn continue -> no results row and no job for the id, and the turn's save is refused. Sweep: with a fake clock, 1,000 sessions idle 7 h -> zero jobs, results, MemoryStore docs and listeners after one sweep; a running job is never removed. Concurrency: 10 research starts -> at most 4 running work functions at once.
designs.risks: A sweep that removes a result a resumed session still needs: touched_at is refreshed on every read and on every turn (touch), and the cutoff equals the session idle expiry, so a live session's rows are never older. The delete timeout path relies on the store's version check rejecting the late save (MemoryStore and SqlStore both do). Semaphores add queueing latency under bursts; the turn already waits only briefly and narrates 'still searching' only for genuinely running jobs.

designs.understanding: novelty.py and scan.py word conclusions without consulting what was actually searched. scan._local wraps the TN startup lookup in 'except Exception: pass' and is not in the coverage list, so a failed or missing ecosystem file returns the same empty list as a genuine no-match; novelty._context then sets gap when tn == 0, the statement says 'I found no Tamil Nadu startup doing it' and the localise lever repeats it, although the map holds 654 startups in 3 metro districts. _statement's fallback 'Each part is well studied, and so are their combinations' fires whenever no part is sparse, even when no pair was counted (one searchable part, or every pair count returned budget_exhausted), and adds the 'business model' lever 'because every part and combination is crowded'. Two matchers over the same 654 records disagree (scan._local: >=2 shared words with an anchor rule; cohort/reference.similar_startups: >=2 shared stems with idf only for ordering and a weaker stoplist), so Talk says 'no TN startup' while the Cohort page lists 20, and the cohort counts filler words (through, developing, patients) as matches. terms.public_vocabulary() takes every word of every registry summary (small, building, local, village...) and build_queries fills papers-query slots with them. scrub() is a blocklist in practice: a model-written word is dropped only if the founder said it verbatim and it is not public vocabulary, so 'KaruvaduKart-style' or 'Karuvadu Kart' leave the device, against decision 0004's allowlist rule. Root cause: no single evidence record says what was searched, in which corpus, with what status, and no single vocabulary decides which words are allowed and which carry meaning.

approaches.name: Evidence record with local-source status + scoped, coverage-aware statements + one shared local matcher with an anchor/idf guard + a document-frequency query vocabulary + an allowlist scrub backed by a committed public technical-term list
approaches.how: The local lookup returns a SourceResult-style record (status ok/not_searched/error, corpus name/size/districts) and joins coverage; novelty statements and levers are generated from that record and from pair-count coverage (attempted vs counted); one matcher module serves scan and cohort, requiring >=1 anchor term with idf above a threshold plus >=2 non-generic shared terms; public_vocabulary splits into an allowlist (may leave) and a query vocabulary (may fill a slot, excluding words with high document frequency across registry summaries); scrub keeps a model word only if every hyphen part is in the allowlist (public vocabulary + an OpenAlex topics/keywords term list committed as data).
approaches.basis: 'Not searched is never nothing found' is the project's own rule (agents/ideation.py coverage note, decision 0005); idf/document-frequency filtering is textbook IR; an allowlist is what decision 0004 specifies; OpenAlex topics are CC0 public data.
approaches.advantages: Fixes the false claims at the wording layer by construction, removes the Talk/Cohort contradiction, enforces 0004 as written, offline and dependency-free.
approaches.drawbacks: Allowlist scrub loses some model terms not in the list (recall), mitigated by the technical-term list; thresholds need eval tuning.

approaches.name: Keep a blocklist scrub with fuzzy matching of founder words (rapidfuzz)
approaches.how: Drop model words that are near-duplicates of non-vocabulary founder words (edit distance, plural/hyphen normalisation).
approaches.drawbacks: A blocklist can always be evaded (split, transliterate, abbreviate); contradicts 0004's allowlist; new dependency.

approaches.name: BM25 ranking (rank_bm25) or scikit-learn TF-IDF for local matching
approaches.how: Score startups by BM25 over descriptions and apply a score threshold.
approaches.drawbacks: A dependency for a ~700-document corpus; score thresholds drift as the corpus grows; does not by itself fix status or wording.

approaches.name: Local embeddings (existing offline hash embedding service / BGE-M3) for similarity
approaches.how: Embed idea and startup descriptions and threshold cosine similarity.
approaches.drawbacks: The offline hash provider is not semantic; BGE-M3 is heavy on CPU and needs a model download; similarity thresholds are opaque to founders, unlike shared words.

approaches.name: Retry failed counts before wording
approaches.how: Re-request pair and context counts until they succeed.
approaches.drawbacks: Spends the scarce free budget and can still fail; the wording must be honest anyway.

approaches.name: Widen the local corpus only (crawl more startups, statewide)
approaches.how: Grow the TN startup data so absence means more.
approaches.drawbacks: Absence is still not proof; the claim must stay scoped whatever the size, so this complements but cannot replace scoped wording.

designs.chosen: Evidence record with local-source status + scoped, coverage-aware statements + one shared local matcher (anchor + idf guard) + document-frequency query vocabulary + allowlist scrub with a committed OpenAlex technical-term list
designs.why_chosen: The false statements are wording decisions made without the evidence record, so the fix is to build the record (status, corpus, what was counted) and derive every sentence from it; that makes 'not searched' impossible to word as 'none found'. One matcher removes the contradiction at its source and gives 1.2.1.3 and 5.5.2 one thing to improve. The allowlist is what decision 0004 says; a committed public technical-term list keeps most model terms. Document frequency removes filler automatically as the registry grows. All offline, no dependency.

not_chosen.reason: Evadable by construction and contrary to 0004's allowlist; adds a dependency.

not_chosen.name: BM25/TF-IDF libraries
not_chosen.reason: Dependency out of proportion for ~700 records; idf is three lines and already computed in cohort/reference.py.

not_chosen.name: Embedding similarity
not_chosen.reason: The offline provider is not semantic and the real model is heavy; shared-word evidence is explainable to founders.

not_chosen.name: Retry before wording
not_chosen.reason: Burns the free budget and still needs honest wording when it fails.

not_chosen.reason: Useful (T09's statewide build helps) but absence still needs scoped wording.

design.components: 1) research/local.py (new, the single matcher): LocalCorpus loaded from ecosystem _meta (name 'Tamil Nadu Startup Map', size, districts, crawled date); match(idea_text, sector=None, limit) -> LocalResult {status: 'ok'|'not_searched'|'error', corpus, matches: [{name, district, shared_terms, score, url}], total}. Rule: shared non-generic terms >= 2 AND at least one shared anchor (a technical term from the lexicon or a term with idf >= ANCHOR_IDF); sector bonus only orders. GENERIC = research/terms.GENERIC plus corpus terms with document frequency above 5% of descriptions. Exceptions are caught, logged (local.error with the class) and returned as status 'error'. 2) scan.py: _local delegates to local.match and adds a coverage row {'source':'local','status':..,'found':..,'note': 'Tamil Nadu Startup Map: N startups in <districts>'}; the research job stores the LocalResult on the session (with the idea version, T06) and the Cohort page reads it for the session (POST /cohort/reference gains an optional session_id; free text keeps working via the same matcher). 3) cohort/reference.py: similar_startups calls local.match; DISTRICTS and the corpus size read from _meta; the 'room to be the local option' observation only when local status is ok and the founder's district is inside the corpus districts, phrased as 'none of the N listed on the map in <district>'. 4) novelty.py: evidence fields pairs_attempted, pairs_counted, context_searched, local {status, corpus}; _statement types: combination | context | element | crowded | crowded_parts_only ('Each part is well studied; I could not count how often they are combined this time') | single_part ('This idea has one searchable part, X, with N papers; I can't judge combinations'); 'context' type and the localise lever require local.status == 'ok' and name the corpus ('none of the 654 startups on the Tamil Nadu Startup Map (Chennai, Coimbatore, Madurai)'); the business-model lever requires pairs_counted >= 1 and every counted pair non-rare. 5) terms.py: public_vocabulary() unchanged in meaning (words allowed to leave) plus TECHNICAL_TERMS from research/data/technical_terms.json (OpenAlex topics display names + keywords, CC0, fetched once by scripts/build_technical_terms.py with _meta source/retrieved); query_vocabulary() = public_vocabulary minus words whose document frequency across registry summaries exceeds QUERY_DF_MAX (10%) minus a reviewed FILLER list (small, building, local, village, people, first, home, cheap ...); build_queries and element_query use query_vocabulary for content slots. 6) scrub(): allowlist: split each model word on hyphens; keep only if every part (lower) is in public_vocabulary or TECHNICAL_TERMS words, and the word is not a place (T10's gazetteer: districts and towns); numbers dropped; at most 8 words. The founder-said rule stays as an extra guard.
design.data_model: LocalResult {status, corpus: {name, size, districts, crawled}, matches, total}. Novelty response adds evidence {pairs_attempted, pairs_counted, context_searched, local_status}. technical_terms.json {"_meta": {source: 'OpenAlex topics (CC0)', retrieved, rows}, "terms": [...lower-cased words and phrases]}. Session stores the local result as an artefact (T11) with the idea version.
design.algorithm: idf(w) = log(N / df(w)); generic(w) = w in GENERIC or df(w)/N > 0.05; accept startup if |shared minus generic| >= 2 and any(w in anchors or idf(w) >= ANCHOR_IDF for w in shared minus generic). Statement selection: if any counted pair is a gap -> combination; elif context_searched and local ok and context gap -> context; elif sparse parts -> element; elif len(searched) == 1 -> single_part; elif pairs_counted == 0 -> crowded_parts_only; else crowded. Scrub: keep(w) = all(p in ALLOW for p in w.lower().split('-')) and not place(w).
design.interfaces: T01: sector values for the matcher's sector bonus come from the canonical vocabulary. T08/T15: SourceResult statuses for remote sources; the local row uses the same status words. T09: statewide ecosystem build changes the corpus districts automatically via _meta. T10: place gazetteer reused by scrub. T11: LocalResult stored as an artefact and cited by the fact ledger. T35: panel seats cite the same evidence record. T33: eval adds degraded fixtures (local error, budget_exhausted pairs, single-part idea).
design.rollout: PR 1: local status + coverage row + scoped context wording (stops the false claim). PR 2: coverage-aware combination statements and lever guards. PR 3: single matcher used by scan and cohort, session-stored result. PR 4: query vocabulary DF filter. PR 5: technical-terms data PR, then allowlist scrub (run the eval to measure recall loss).

designs.understanding: config.secret_key defaults to 'change-me' and nothing refuses it outside development (is_production is defined but unused), so any deployment that forgets SECRET_KEY accepts tokens anyone can mint. Refresh tokens are issued but the frontend never calls /auth/refresh (api.ts sends only the access token; auth.tsx drops tokens on any /me failure), refresh_token_pair reissues without invalidating the old token, jti is never stored, and there is no logout, so founders are signed out every 30 minutes and a stolen refresh token stays valid 14 days. authenticate_user short-circuits 'user is None or not verify_password', skipping bcrypt for unknown emails (timing oracle) despite its comment, and register answers 409 EMAIL_TAKEN. RateLimitMiddleware keys by request.state.user_id, which nothing sets, so every request is keyed by request.client.host: founders behind carrier-grade NAT or one reverse proxy share 100/min, every /voice/speak and notices reconnect counts the same as a turn, a 429 on the EventSource kills notices silently, the per-client dict is never pruned, and limits are per process. Root cause: auth was built as a demo (no secret guard, stateless tokens with no server record) and the limiter has no notion of identity or route cost.

approaches.name: Harden in place: settings validator + key ring, refresh-token table with rotation and reuse detection, constant-work login, and an identity-aware cost-class limiter with a memory/Redis counter backend
approaches.how: A Pydantic model_validator refuses default/short secrets outside development; tokens carry kid so a previous key verifies during rotation. A refresh_tokens table (hashed jti, family, expires, revoked, replaced_by) makes refresh rotate tokens and revoke a family on reuse; logout revokes the family; api.ts retries once after a single-flight refresh on 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED. Login verifies against a dummy hash for unknown emails; auth routes get a tight per-IP+email bucket. The limiter resolves an identity (user from a verified bearer token without DB, else session id from agent/voice paths, else client IP honouring X-Forwarded-For only from trusted proxies), applies route cost classes (turn, speak, stream-open, auth, default) plus an IP backstop and the global cap, and counts in fixed windows in memory (pruned) or Redis (INCR+EXPIRE).
approaches.basis: OWASP ASVS session-management guidance, OAuth 2.0 Security BCP (refresh token rotation with reuse detection), python-jose and passlib already installed, the INCR+EXPIRE pattern already used in research/sources.py.
approaches.advantages: No new dependency; works with or without Redis; per-user and per-session limits match how founders connect; revocation lives in the same database as users (auth needs the DB anyway).
approaches.drawbacks: A migration (T16 chain) and frontend changes; limiter code to maintain.

approaches.name: fastapi-users (or Authlib) for auth
approaches.how: Replace the auth module with a library providing register/login/refresh/logout and token strategies.
approaches.drawbacks: Rewrites working auth and models, migration of users, a large dependency surface; the secret guard and limiter are still ours.

approaches.name: Redis denylist of revoked jti
approaches.how: Store revoked jti in Redis with TTL until expiry; check on refresh.
approaches.drawbacks: Redis is optional, so revocation silently disappears when it is off; no reuse detection; nothing to delete with the user under 3.2.4.

approaches.name: slowapi / limits library for rate limiting
approaches.how: Decorate routes with limits and pick a storage backend.
approaches.advantages: Moving windows, decorators, ready storage backends.
approaches.drawbacks: The async Redis storage of limits needs a second Redis client (coredis); still needs our keying decision (user/session/IP) and cost classes; route decorators spread policy across routers.

approaches.name: Reverse proxy or edge rate limiting (nginx limit_req, Caddy, Cloudflare free tier)
approaches.how: Enforce limits before the app.
approaches.advantages: Protects the app process itself; no app code.
approaches.drawbacks: Hosting is undecided and the offline/local setup has no proxy; edge limits see only IPs (the CGNAT problem) and cannot see sessions or users.

approaches.name: httpOnly secure cookies for tokens with CSRF protection
approaches.how: Move tokens from localStorage to cookies set by the server.
approaches.basis: OWASP recommendation against token theft via XSS.
approaches.drawbacks: Does not provide revocation, rotation or logout on its own; needs CSRF handling and SameSite care across the Vite dev proxy; a worthwhile later hardening, not the fix for these flags.

designs.chosen: Harden in place: settings validator with a two-key ring, refresh-token table with rotation/reuse detection/logout and a 401-retry client, constant-work login with an auth bucket, and an identity-aware, cost-class rate limiter with pruned memory counters and an optional Redis INCR+EXPIRE backend
designs.why_chosen: Each flag is a missing server-side record or check, and every fix fits the existing modules with libraries already installed. The database is already required for auth, so a refresh-token table gives revocation that cannot silently vanish (unlike a Redis denylist) and is erasable with the user. Identity-aware keys are the only way to stop shared-IP lockouts without weakening protection, and cost classes stop TTS and reconnects from eating the turn budget. Reusing the research budget's INCR+EXPIRE pattern keeps one counter idiom in the codebase and works without Redis.

not_chosen.name: slowapi / limits
not_chosen.reason: Async Redis storage needs a second client library, and the keying and cost-class decisions remain ours; decorators scatter policy.

not_chosen.name: Proxy/edge limiting
not_chosen.reason: Hosting is undecided, the local setup has no proxy, and edges see only IPs, which is the bug.

not_chosen.reason: Good later hardening but provides no revocation or rotation; recorded as a follow-up, not this theme's fix.

design.components: 1) core/config.py: model_validator(mode='after'): if app_env != 'development' and (secret_key in {'change-me', '', 'secret', 'changeme'} or len(secret_key) < 32) -> ValueError naming SECRET_KEY; optional secret_key_previous (verify only). core/security.py: tokens carry header kid = sha256(key)[:8]; decode tries the key whose kid matches (current, then previous). docs/runbooks/rotate-key.md: SECRET_KEY section (generate, set previous, deploy, remove previous after refresh_token_expire_days; what happens to sessions). 2) models/refresh_token.py + Alembic migration (T16 chain): refresh_tokens(jti_hash char(64) PK, user_id FK users ON DELETE CASCADE, family_id uuid, issued_at, expires_at, revoked_at null, replaced_by null); index (user_id), (family_id). services/auth_service.py: issue_token_pair(user, family=None) stores sha256(jti); refresh_token_pair: decode, look up row; if missing or expired -> 401; if revoked -> reuse detected: revoke whole family, log auth.refresh_reuse, 401 (except a 30 s grace when replaced_by was issued moments ago, for concurrent tabs); else mark revoked + replaced_by and issue a new pair in the same family. logout(refresh_token) revokes the family; routers/auth.py adds POST /auth/logout (204). Cleanup of expired rows runs in T32's maintenance runner. 3) frontend/src/api.ts: on 401 with error_code TOKEN_EXPIRED, one shared in-flight refresh promise, store the new pair, retry the original request once; on refresh failure clear tokens and surface 'signed out'. auth.tsx: logout() calls /auth/logout before clearing; startup /me failure with TOKEN_EXPIRED tries refresh instead of dropping tokens. 4) authenticate_user: ok = verify_password(password, user.hashed_password if user else DUMMY_HASH) (DUMMY_HASH computed once at import with the same bcrypt cost); if user is None or not ok -> 401. Register keeps its helpful 409 (no email channel exists to send 'check your inbox'), but /auth/* gets the 'auth' cost class keyed by IP and by email hash (10 per 15 minutes) to slow enumeration; revisit when email verification exists. 5) core/ratelimit.py (new) + middleware: identity(request) -> ('user', sub) if a Bearer token verifies (decode_token, no DB; invalid tokens fall through to IP, never error here) | ('session', id) for /api/v1/ideation/agent/sessions/{id}/* and voice routes carrying a session id | ('ip', client_ip) where client_ip honours X-Forwarded-For only when request.client.host is in settings.trusted_proxies. Route classes from a table of path patterns: turn (POST .../turns, .../turns/stream) 20/min per identity; speak (/api/v1/voice/speak) 120/min per identity; stream_open (.../notices) 12/min per identity; auth (/api/v1/auth/*) 10/15 min per ip+email; default 100/min per identity; ip_backstop 600/min per client IP for every request; global 1000/min per process (unchanged). 6) Counter backend: fixed 60 s windows; MemoryCounter dict[(class, key, window)] -> int, dropping all entries of older windows on rollover (bounded by active keys in one window); RedisCounter INCR + EXPIRE on 'rl:{class}:{key}:{window}' when get_redis() is up, falling back to memory on error. 429 responses carry retry-after = seconds to window end and a 'limit_class' field; every 429 logs ratelimit.rejected with class and identity kind (never the raw id) for T23. 7) frontend/src/voice/agentClient.ts: listenNotices onerror -> close and reopen after a back-off (2 s, 5 s, 15 s, cap 60 s), so a 429 or network blip no longer kills notices.
design.data_model: refresh_tokens as above. Settings: secret_key_previous: str|None, trusted_proxies: list[str] = [], rate_limits: dict[class, (limit, window_s)] with defaults above. JWT header kid.
design.algorithm: Refresh rotation with reuse detection (OAuth 2.0 Security BCP): one active token per family; presenting a revoked token outside the grace window revokes the family. Limiter: for each request, classes = [route_class, 'ip_backstop', 'global']; key = identity for the route class / client ip / '*'; count = incr(class, key, window); if count > limit -> 429 for that class. Fixed windows keep counters O(active keys).
design.interfaces: T17 (session identity and ownership) consumes the verified user identity and the session-id keying; when T17 adds owner checks the limiter's session key can become user-or-session. T16 owns the migration chain for refresh_tokens. T32 erasure deletes refresh_tokens via the user FK cascade and its runner purges expired rows. T23 receives ratelimit.rejected and auth.refresh_reuse events. T28's client queue cooperates with the notices reopen. T18 owns browser token storage keys (vanigam_* registry). T08's Redis re-probe benefits the limiter's Redis backend.

designs.tests: Security: production settings with the default or a 16-char key raise at startup; a token signed with 'change-me' is rejected in production config; rotation: token signed with the previous key verifies while SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS is set and fails after removal. Login timing: mean duration for unknown vs known email within 20%. Refresh: refresh returns a new pair and the old refresh token then fails; replaying a revoked token after the grace window revokes the family (the newest token also fails); logout makes the refresh token fail; expired rows ignored. Limiter: 30 clients with distinct bearer tokens behind one IP each get their own 'default' budget; 20 sessions behind one IP can each take turns; /voice/speak bursts do not reduce the turn bucket; 700 requests/min from one IP hit the backstop; memory counter size returns to zero after two idle windows; with fakeredis two middleware instances share a count; X-Forwarded-For ignored unless the peer is a trusted proxy. Frontend: api.ts retries once after refresh (mocked fetch); notices reopen after a 429.
designs.risks: Decoding the bearer token in middleware costs a signature check per request (microseconds for HS256); invalid tokens must never raise in middleware. Session-id keying can be evaded by minting sessions; the IP backstop and the session-creation route's own class bound it, and T17's ownership checks tighten it. Refresh rotation with concurrent tabs can trigger false reuse detection: the client's single-flight refresh and the 30 s grace mitigate. Migration depends on T16's frozen chain.
